newsitem.title: UK: Eurobonds see surge of five-year dollar deals.
newsitem.headline: Eurobonds see surge of five-year dollar deals.

text.p: Five-year dollar bonds proved to be the flavour of the day on Wednesday, with sizeable fixed transactions and also some FRNs seen.
Landesgirokasse Oeffentliche Bank and Landesparkasse (LGK) launched its dollar benchmark bond, a $500 million five-year deal, which paid 13 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes.

The triple-A rated German bank had held an extensive roadshow in Asia and Europe before launching the deal, and a syndicate manager at joint lead CSFB said the transaction had been well-received as a result.
"LGK is a rare name in the market, and spent a lot of time educating investors," the CSFB syndicate manager said.
"The deal has had a good start, with buying from Asian funds and European accounts."
He said the extra supply in the market provided by a $500 million five-year bond for Morgan Guaranty Trust Co New York had not hampered sales.
"The market is well-bid at the moment," he said.
MGT's bond, self-led via J.P. Morgan, was priced to yield 18 b.p. over Treasuries.
Bankers said both the LGK and MGT deals were fairly priced.
"MGT looked the fairest of all in terms of pricing, and it is a name that attracts both institutions and retail," a trader at a European bank said.
"It can even be seen as cheap relative to where other AA1/AAA names are trading. LGK also compares well with other German bank paper," he said.
In the floater market, Associates Corp of North America launched a $500 million five-year FRN, priced at a discount margin of 10 basis points over three-month Libor.
"The deal was priced at the wide end of the indicated range, and this level looks fine," said an FRN trader at a U.S. bank.
"Associates Corp remains bid at the reoffer level."

Although the deal has a Euro-Asian format, with listings in Europe and Asia to appeal to investors in both regions, dealers said there was relatively little buying of FRNs by Asian investors, who preferred high-quality fixed-rate paper.
The lead managers J.P. Morgan and Morgan Stanley were not immediately available for comment.
More supply is expected in the dollar market, with Sweden said to be eyeing a seven-year deal for up to $500 million. Spread talk was around 20 b.p. over five-year Treasuries.
"Spreads are tight, and many borrowers are looking to take advantage of attractive borrowing costs," a dealer at a German bank said.
"To get yields, investors are moving out along the yield curve, from three to five years and from five to seven years," he said.
U.S. Treasury bonds were steady in London on Wednesday ahead of what dealers said was likely to be a successful auction of 10-year notes.
Early weakness in the dollar against the yen had tempted some Japanese investors into Treasuries, analysts said.
Many continental European countries will be out of the market on Thursday due to Ascension Day holidays.
-- Aline van Duyn, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7748
